description.narrative: "DON'T PUB DROP 1. Why was code established and nature of the work In 1999comma the Eastern Nile (EN) riparian'scomma including Egyptcomma Ethiopia and Sudancomma agreed to establish an investment oriented program referred to as the Eastern Nile Subsidiary Action Program (ENSAP) under the framework of the Nile Basin Initiative (NBI). In 2001comma by the EN countries reached consensus that the first ENSAP 'project' comma referred to as the Integrated Development of the Eastern Nile (IDEN) projectcomma would ""initiate a regionalcomma integratedcomma multipurpose development project through a first set of investments to confer tangible benefits# and demonstrate joint action."" This first set of agreed investments included 7 'subprojects: ' - Irrigation & Drainage - Ethiopia-Sudan Interconnections - Flood Preparedness and Early Warning - Watershed Management - EN Power Trade Investment studies - EN Planning Model - Baro-Akobo multipurpose water resources development The IDEN Facilitation code was established in FY02 to provide technical assistance to the EN Regional Technical Office (ENTRO)comma a newly formed sub-regional NBI project office for the Eastern Nilecomma and facilitate project preparation activitiescomma as well as support institutional development to their nascent office. In parallel to the Bank-executed IDEN Facilitation codecomma a PHRD grant of $1.5 million (2003-2007) was obtained for client-executed activities related to project preparationcomma particularly related to the EN Planning Modelcomma Flood Preparednesscomma and the Ethiopia-Sudan Interconnection. Client-executed project preparation activities were also supplemented by GEF and NBTF-financed grants to ENTRO for watershed management and other IDEN activities. Some projectscomma such as the Power Trade studiescomma where supported bilaterally by other Partners (i.e.comma AfDB). The IDEN Facilitation supported Bank staff (Bankcomma co-termcomma etc) and consultantscomma and related expenses (travelcomma workshopscomma technical consultanciescomma etc)comma required to facilitate dialogue and build consensus among the EN countriescomma assist in institutional development of ENTROcomma and to support and review project preparation activities. An integrated approach was required in the early yearscomma the historic tensions among these countriescomma the need to build harmonized project preparation approaches for this new entitycomma and riparian preference. 2. Why the code was closed As ENTRO matured and project preparation activities advancedcomma a decision was made to 'spin -off' IDEN 'subprojects' as individual projectscomma with individual preparation and/or lending codes. As projects were ready and alternative funding mechanisms were put in placecomma all IDEN projects were 'spun off.' This included separate codes for investment oriented projects (and associated project preparation related activities)comma as well as for institutional strengthening (and associated 'facilitation' and institutional strengthening activities). The IDEN Facilitation code was last used in FY05."
